answer: Every identity locks a bond before acting—perhaps timber harvested from a terrace above the glacier—held in escrow. Since each clone needs its own costly deposit, a sybil swarm must tie up real value per identity. Watchers fingerprint behavior and challenge suspected duplicates. If a challenge proves two identities share one operator, slashing seizes both bonds automatically. Honest agents recover deposits when they exit; mass impersonation becomes too expensive to sustain.
